person.their note: It's 2am and I keep replaying a conversation from 2019 in my head, what I said and what I should have said. I can't switch it off.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: Your mind keeps replaying a conversation from 2019, and this restless monkey reaches even where it cannot go.

week 1.verse line: Craving is a restless monkey: never in one place, never satisfied, reaching even where it cannot go.
week 1.personal line written for them: That conversation from 2019 is not a place you can go, and it is not a place you can stay. The mind that keeps replaying it is the restless monkey. You can let it go for this day.

week 1.verse line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is giving the same old scene fuel at 2am. You do not have to watch it burn.

week 1.verse line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are caught in the loop of a past conversation, replaying every word. The mind is trying to fix what is already finished. Peace is not in finding the right thing to say. Peace is in letting the fruit of that moment go.

week 1.verse line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep replaying that 2019 conversation at 2am. The mind is a monkey, and it is allowed to jump. You do not have to wrestle it into silence tonight.

week 1.verse line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.

week 1.story: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
week 1.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
week 1.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
week 1.personal line written for them: That conversation from 2019 keeps replaying at two in the morning because you are still asking what it means. The mind will not stay still by force. You can return to it with patience and ask what you are in that moment.

week 2.verse line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind runs here and there for nothing, like a stray village dog. The conversation from 2019 is just a sound it keeps chasing. Let it wander without following.

week 2.verse line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind replays that old conversation, caught in the current of hope. The water is wish, the waves are craving, and the banks are worry. You are not on the far shore today.

week 2.verse line: I don't refuse good things that come to me, and I don't chase what's hard to get.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind replays 2019, but the past is already held. Let the conversation rest. The mind that stops chasing what is lost finds what is present.

week 2.verse line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your peace does not depend on a reply from the past. The replaying is the waiting. Let the expectation go and sleep.

week 2.verse line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
week 2.personal line written for them: That voice at 2am is still arguing with a version of you from 2019. You can let the replay fade without fixing what it said. Steady resolve is enough to quiet it tonight.

week 2.verse line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is a room where a conversation from 2019 is playing on loop, and you are standing in its doorway, unable to leave. The verse says to stop wandering and rest somewhere. Let the night pass without replaying what was said, and let the morning come without scripting what should be said.

week 2.story: Kabir to his own restless mind: slowly, slowly
week 2.summary: The mind wants the result now. Kabir talks to it the way a gardener would.
week 2.lesson: Water faithfully; the fruit comes in its season, not because you poured more.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are replaying a conversation from years ago, trying to force a result that is no longer in your hands. You keep pouring water into the past, but the fruit of that moment will not ripen on your schedule. Let the water be enough today, and let the season be its own.

week 3.verse line: Every good quality I take up, craving gnaws through, like a mouse chewing a string.
week 3.personal line written for them: You sit in the dark with a conversation from years ago. The mind chews on what was said and what was not. No quality holds when the craving gnaws.

week 3.verse line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
week 3.personal line written for them: That replay from 2019 is still running in the body. Step back from the body, and rest as the awareness watching it. You can be calm and free right now.

week 3.verse line: Sit like a witness, unshaken, knowing it's just moods moving through, and stay steady.
An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
week 3.personal line written for them: The mind keeps replaying that 2019 conversation because it is still trying to finish the sentence. It is not a mistake you made; it is a thought that is still working.

week 3.verse line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
week 3.personal line written for them: That 2019 conversation still has its hooks in you. The outer work of your life keeps piling up. You can stay turned inward while it does, and the sense of being the doer will fall away.

week 3.story: Bhima cannot bear to wait thirteen years
week 3.summary: Bhima is sick of waiting. The years we wait, he tells Yudhishthira, are years off our lives, and death does not pause for a pledge. He even offers a scholar's loophole: the texts allow a substitute, so count the thirteen months we have already lived here as thirteen years, and let us go and...
week 3.lesson: A pledge is not broken by a clever reading of it; time that must be waited out can be spent getting ready.
week 3.personal line written for them: The past conversation replays because it is unfinished. The waiting for a better answer can become the work of finding it. You are preparing for the next time you speak.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: I can't stop overthinking

week 1.verse line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is running long after the workday ends, and that restlessness is exhausting. The text does not ask you to stop the thoughts. It says the mind is strong and stubborn by nature. You can train it by returning to one thing again and again.

week 1.verse line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are not the mind; thoughts come and go before the silent witness that watches them and is never disturbed.

week 1.verse line: A churned-up lake settles and clears on its own. So does a mind, given time.
week 1.personal line written for them: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind. But the verse tells us that a churned-up lake settles and clears on its own. Your work is not a throne you have lost. It is the ground you stand on right now.

week 1.verse line: Sorrow, craving and unbearable anxiety all vanish in a calm mind, like darkness before the sun.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind runs in circles because it was never taught to rest. It is not a flaw. It is a habit that has grown too strong. Choose calm for a moment. Let the darkness of worry fade without fighting it. The restlessness will slow down on its own.

week 1.verse line: Daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been trying to force your mind to stop, but it is not a problem to be fixed today. It is a fruit that needs time. Keep doing your ordinary work, and let the ripening happen on its own.

week 1.verse line: Let go of old cravings, speak only what heals, and live in the present.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is restless because it is still pulling at old cravings, maybe for a different result at work or for a sense of control you cannot have. The restlessness is not a flaw in you. It is the mind still reaching for something that is not this moment.

week 1.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 1.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 1.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 1.personal line written for them: Janaka heard the sages and climbed to his roof to question his life, but he did not abandon the palace. You are not required to leave your desk to find a quieter mind. The work is still there, but it can be held by a mind that does not clutch.

week 2.verse line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind keeps a running tally of every task and worry, and it never clears the screen. You are not broken. You are caught in the same endless list Vilasa named. Let the tally exist without running it. Let the mind rest in the space between the items.

week 2.verse line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
week 2.personal line written for them: The lists in your head are not the problem. They are just the noise of a mind that was never taught to rest. What you feel is not a failure of your will.

week 2.verse line: Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is running the show, pulling you toward every unfinished task and every what-if. That is the wild horse you are trying to ride. The thought that you are the rider is still there, waiting. You can feel the reins in your hands.

week 2.verse line: Friend mind, why all this chatter? It's all speculation. You are vast as the sky.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are not the mind; thoughts come and go before the silent witness that watches them and is never disturbed.

week 2.verse line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
week 2.personal line written for them: The lists of what you did, what you are doing, and what you could do keep the mind from resting. It is not your fault. The mind simply needs to be brought back, not punished. Bring your attention back to the breath, and let the lists wait for the evening.

week 2.verse line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are working, and the work is real. The mind races because it thinks the work is the only thing that matters. Ribhu shows that you can be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. You can do the work at hand and let go of what is lost.

week 2.story: Bali tires of endless days and asks his father's riddle
week 2.summary: The demon king Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day at his window he realises he is doing the same things day after day, night after night, and asks what any of it adds up to. He remembers a riddle his father Virochana once told him: a vast realm ruled by a silent king and an...
week 2.lesson: When life feels like a loop, the work is not more of it but mastering the mind that runs it.

week 3.verse line: You are not your body or your achievements. You are the awareness watching it all. Live lightly.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind keeps running because it thinks it is the doer, the one who must fix and figure everything out. It is not. You are the awareness in which these thoughts rise and fall. Let the overthinking be the waves. You are the ocean.

week 3.verse line: The mind is a wicker basket in water: pour in riches, and it still never fills.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your work keeps giving you things to do, but the restlessness does not leave. You are sitting at your desk and the mind is still empty. The basket is still wet. What you are feeling is the truth of the basket.

week 3.verse line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind races because it thinks it has to own every thought. But the thoughts are just clouds moving through the sky of your awareness. You are not the racing, you are the space where it happens. Let this awareness be your steady ground today.

week 3.verse line: Calm, self-controlled, quiet within, patient and collected: that is how you come to see clearly.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind is running on the idea that it must produce to be worthy. This teaching asks you to see your worth as something that does not grow or shrink with your output. Let the restlessness be there without letting it run the show.

week 3.verse line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind has been running on the day's work without a pause. You can step away from the noise for a few minutes and let your senses rest. This is not about forcing your thoughts to stop. It is about letting your mind settle on one thing.

week 3.verse line: Don't chase your pleasures and pains. Know the one who feels them.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind is running through every task and worry without a single pause. The Upanishad suggests you stop chasing the noise. You do not need to fix the thoughts or force them away. You only need to notice the one who is watching them. That quiet observer is already there.

week 3.story: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
week 3.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow...
week 3.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have spent years believing that a restless mind is a mind that is working hard. It is not. It is a mind that has never been taught to stop running.

person.their note: Promotion results come out next month and I can't stop thinking about it. I check my manager's calendar, I rehearse the conversation, I can't enjoy anything until I know.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

week 1.verse line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind will not settle, and that is the weight you carry right now. The mind cannot be forced into silence.

week 1.verse line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are carrying the weight of the whole outcome in your head, as if the work succeeds or fails only because you do. You are one cause among five. Your part is the effort you put in, not the final result.

week 1.verse line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your part is the effort, not the outcome; work done well is already complete, whatever result comes.

week 1.verse line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are trying to rest before the work is done, as if your mind could settle only when the outcome is certain. The verse shows a mind that is already full, not because the work is finished, but because it does not beg for a different result.

week 1.verse line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is restless because you are trying to finish the work in your head before the day is done. The work is only on the outside. Let the doing be enough. Busy outside, unhurried inside.

week 1.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your work is yours to do. The results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop. You are caught in the loop of waiting for the outcome before you let yourself rest. The work is the only thing you control. Let the rest go.

week 1.story: Hanuman's search and near despair
week 1.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.
week 1.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
week 1.personal line written for them: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: Your mind won't settle while you are working, and a verse was chosen with that weight in mind.

week 1.verse line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is caught in a net of reckonings, checking calendars and rehearsing conversations it cannot control.

week 1.verse line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are rehearsing a conversation that has not happened yet. The spinning is keeping your world small. Let the calendar stay blank for a little while.

week 1.verse line: No winter was but summer came behind,
week 1.personal line written for them: The waiting for your promotion results is a heavy winter that feels endless right now, but the text reminds us that no winter stays. Light and shade only push each other along. Let yourself be steady in this waiting.

week 1.verse line: 'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are caught in a fever of what might come, rehearsing a future that is not here. The promotion is not decided, and the conversation has not happened. You can set down the worry and let today be a place to rest.

week 1.verse line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are rehearsing a conversation that is not yet here. The work in front of you is what is happening right now. Let the promotion results come when they come; they do not need your worry to arrive.

week 1.verse line: If I say anything wrong, stop me. Don't be afraid.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is rehearsing every possible outcome until the results arrive. You are allowed to let the outcome be unknown. Rest in the fact that your worth is not decided by a promotion.

week 1.story: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
week 1.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow...
week 1.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is rehearsing a conversation that has not happened yet. The worry about next month is a fire that is burning your present. You can step back from the rehearsal and simply watch the breath coming in and going out.

person.their note: My best friend got into Harvard today. I congratulated her and then went and cried in the bathroom. I hate that I feel this way.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: You hate that you feel this way, yet understanding Bharat's advice does not bring your heart to rest.

week 1.verse line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
week 1.personal line written for them: You understand that your friend deserves this, yet your own chest feels hollow. The advice to be happy for her meets a heart that is not at peace. Let your heart have its say without needing to fix it now.

week 1.verse line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
You torment yourself with shame for nothing. In my eyes you stand above them all.
week 1.personal line written for them: You sit with a feeling that something does not sit right after your friend's news. You do not have to carry this shame alone. The hurt you feel is not the whole truth about who you are.

week 1.verse line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your own path is the only one that can fit you. It is not wrong to feel the ache of another's success while you walk your own road. Let your own work be enough today.

week 1.verse line: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are allowed to feel what you feel when your friend succeeds. The good in her win can be yours without becoming her. Let your own growth stand beside her path.

week 1.verse line: Don't punish the whole world for one person's wrong.
week 1.personal line written for them: You can hold the ache of your friend's success and your own quiet loss. That feeling does not make you a bad person. Let your anger aim at the real cause of your hurt.

week 1.story: Guha nearly fights Bharat
week 1.summary: Seeing Bharat's army approach the Ganga, Guha assumes he is coming to kill Ram and prepares his men to die fighting. An old man reads the omens and says Bharat comes to bring Ram back. Guha agrees that fools act in haste and repent, goes to meet Bharat with gifts, and the two embrace.
week 1.lesson: Find out someone's intent before you prepare for war with them.
week 1.personal line written for them: You hate the feeling in the bathroom, and that is a sign of care. The fool acts at once and regrets it. Let the feeling sit before you do anything with it.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: I feel jealous of someone close to me

week 1.verse line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are sitting with your books and comparing your progress to the people next to you. The texts say the wise are beyond envy. Your worth is not a scoreboard. Let your work be your own path, not a race against theirs.

week 1.verse line: Most of us swell only at our own rise. Rare is the one who surges at another's.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are in a room with books and screens, and someone close to you has just done something bright. You feel the old tightness in your chest, as if their light is pushing your own into shadow. That is the pond.

week 1.verse line: You torment yourself with guilt for nothing. No one is dearer to Ram than you.
week 1.personal line written for them: You feel small because you measure your study against your friend's. But your worth is not a grade you could chase. It is already full, even in the quiet of your own room. Your part is to trust what you already carry.

week 1.verse line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is making your life small by measuring it against another's. You are not just a student, a friend, or a body. You are the awareness that holds all of it. Your worth is not smaller than theirs. It is not larger either. It is simply there, untouched.

week 1.verse line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are studying and you keep measuring your progress against the people around you. You see their strengths and your own feels small. But your own path is not a borrowed life. Your work is your own, and its worth is not decided by how it looks next to theirs.

week 1.verse line: Make peace with other people's success, even when you lack it. The wise can enjoy good fortune that isn't theirs.
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep looking at the life of a friend and feeling your own days shrink. The sage is saying that your jealousy is not a signal to change your path, it is a weight you are carrying.

week 1.story: Uttanka confronts Krishna
week 1.summary: Returning home after the war, Krishna meets the sage Uttanka, who is furious that Krishna let the cousins destroy each other and threatens to curse him. Krishna explains that he tried hard for peace and was refused, and calms him.
week 1.lesson: You can try your best for peace and still fail. Others' choices are not your guilt.
week 1.personal line written for them: Uttanka wanted to punish Krishna for the war. You want to punish yourself for a feeling you did not choose. Krishna told him he tried hard for peace and was refused. You can try to be kind to yourself and still feel the shame.

person.their note: I lost my father three weeks ago. I keep asking what happens when we die. Is he somewhere? Will I see him again?

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I lost a parent

week 1.verse line: Whoever rests their heart in me, I lift out of the drowning sea, and soon.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are searching for what it is all for after losing a parent. The texts call this the ocean of endless change. Krishna offers to be the lifter, not the answer. You do not have to find the depth alone.

week 1.verse line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
week 1.personal line written for them: You wake up, you go to work, you are with your family. You pass through deep sleep every night and meet something vast, but you do not know it. You are looking for what it is all for, and it is already under your feet.

week 1.verse line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been walking over buried gold for a while, and now the ground beneath your feet feels unsteady. The search for what it is all for has left you with very little time that is your own.

week 1.verse line: The Lord is hidden in your own heart. By his grace one sees him, and sorrow lifts.
week 1.personal line written for them: The grief and fear of death you carry are searching for a place to land. The text offers no quick fix, only the quiet possibility that the answer is already where you sit, beneath the noise of work and family.

week 1.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are working and raising your children, and you have lost a parent. The weight of it is there. The verse does not ask you to stop working or to detach from your family. It says to keep working, but to hold it lightly.

week 1.verse line: Start the day by greeting your mother and father. Small daily respect adds up to a good life.
week 1.personal line written for them: The searching you are living with is a search for what it is all for. You are carrying the weight of work and the children, and the grief of losing a parent. Bhishma says the foundation of a good life is small daily respect.

week 1.story: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
week 1.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the...
week 1.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

week 2.verse line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
week 2.personal line written for them: The weight you carry does not come from a single bad day. It is the slow drying out of your own senses, the sense that nothing you have won or built will touch this. You have reached a place where you cannot tell the right choice from the wrong one.

week 2.verse line: Each sunrise takes a day from us, and, busy with work, we never notice time slipping by.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are busy with work and your family. The days move fast, and you do not notice them slipping by. The grief of losing your parent is still there. Notice the time that is passing, and let your hands rest from the tasks for a moment.

week 2.verse line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are grieving the one you lost, and the grief feels like it will never end. Lakshman is telling Ram that trouble comes to everyone and passes. Your work and your children are still there, but the hole left behind is real. Trouble is not a sign you are weak.

week 2.verse line: Knowing what stays steady inside all that changes, the wise do not grieve.
week 2.personal line written for them: The grief you are drying up inside is for the body, the parent you knew. What they most were is not gone. You can hold on to the idea that what is real does not die. A quiet, honest life is enough to find it.

week 2.verse line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
week 2.personal line written for them: The search you feel is not a lack of answers, but a shift in where you place your life. Your work and your care for your family are the ground you stand on. You do not need to leave them to find what you are looking for.

week 2.verse line: Put the effort you spend earning money into growing wiser first.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are still doing the work, but the mind is tired of the old reasons. The effort you put into earning a living can also be the effort that grows your understanding. The same hands that manage the house and the job can hold a steadier view.

week 2.summary: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having...
week 2.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.
week 2.personal line written for them: Satyakama went to his teacher with nothing but the truth about where he came from. You are looking for a deeper ground to stand on, and the first step is admitting you do not have all the answers yet. Let your children see you searching honestly rather than performing certainty.

week 3.verse line: The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
week 3.personal line written for them: You are sitting in a life full of weight, the work and the children, and the loss of your parent has left you looking for something that will not leave. The verse reminds you that you are not the body that was lost, nor the roles you play.

week 3.verse line: It is the very flavour of life. Whoever tastes it is filled with joy.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are looking for something to hold onto after losing a parent, and you are afraid of what comes after. You have been looking outside yourself, in your work, in your family, for an answer. This teaching says the answer is not a thing to find.

week 3.verse line: Throne or begging bowl, gain or loss, crowd or solitude: a steady person stays the same.
week 3.personal line written for them: The life you carry right now, with its work and its children and its own small moments, is the very place where this steadiness is meant to live. You are not looking for a new room or a new job to feel at peace.

week 3.verse line: The sun shows every flaw yet stays untouched. Your deepest self stays untouched by the world's sorrow.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are looking for something deeper to hold onto after losing a parent. The grief is real, but it is not the whole of you. What stays is not out there among passing things. It is the part of you that remains when the body and the roles change.

week 3.verse line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are holding the weight of the house, the office, and the people who need you, and the searching has made that weight feel heavier than it is. The texts call this the outer work that comes to you, and they say you can do it all without burning out.

week 3.verse line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are doing the outer work of your life and the inner work of your grief at the same time. The verse suggests that the path forward is not to stop the outer work, but to keep the mind attached to the one constant.

week 3.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 3.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 3.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 3.personal line written for them: King Janaka heard a song that shook his certainty about his throne. He did not abandon his garden or his doorkeeper. He simply stopped clutching. You are not asked to leave your work or your grief behind.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: You keep asking where your father is now, and you see no kingdom or lordship that could dry up this grief.

week 1.verse line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are asking where your father is after he died three weeks ago. Your mind cannot find a way forward, and no answer about a kingdom or the gods can reach this hollow in you.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
week 1.verse line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is caught between a father who is gone and a world that will not stop turning. There is no third place for your pain to hide. Let it be only two things, and let the rest of the day be quiet.

week 1.verse line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are asking where he is, and the world feels empty. Trouble touches every living being, like fire, and passes in a moment. The darkness will not last forever.

week 1.verse line: Your wisdom isn't gone. Grief has only put it to sleep for a while.
Steadiness comes from doing. No one becomes steady without acting; act, and steadiness follows.
Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are asking what happens after death, and you do not know which way to go. In this helplessness, you can still hold to the people who steady you. Let their presence be your way forward today.

week 1.story: Hanuman reaches Sita
week 1.summary: Sita, captive and threatened by Ravana, has nearly lost hope; only the guard Trijata has been kind. Hanuman drops Ram's ring from a tree, then tells her Ram's whole story. Sita says he has been her ship in a sea of separation; he gives her Ram's message that speaking of pain helps, but there is...
week 1.lesson: When someone is near despair, a message that they are remembered can carry them.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are asking what happens when we die, and if he is somewhere. Speaking this pain out loud lessens it, and the love that stays with him carries the message even now.

week 2.verse line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your father's absence leaves you asking what happens after death. That confusion is the trap the verse names. You do not have to know the answer today.

week 2.verse line: Without good company, there is no clear judgement.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are asking what happens after death while your father is still fresh in your mind. In this moment, your questions are a heavy fog. Good company is the root of joy and well-being.

week 2.verse line: "Comfort" is no test of truth; on the contrary, truth is often far from being "comfortable"
week 2.personal line written for them: You lost your father three weeks ago. You keep asking if he is somewhere, if you will see him again. The answer you want is not the one that is true. The truth is that comfort is no test of truth, and what you feel is not comfort.

week 2.verse line: When unsure what to do, respectfully ask someone older and wiser. You won't go astray.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are asking where your father is, and the path ahead feels hidden. In this dark, you can ask a trusted friend or elder to sit with you. Their steady presence will keep you from losing your way.

week 2.verse line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
week 2.personal line written for them: The ache of asking where your father is is a real cold that has come. It will pass, as all sense contacts do. Let this thought rest with you today.

week 2.story: Vidura's parable: the man in the well, licking honey
week 2.summary: The old king has lost a hundred sons in eighteen days and lies on the ground. He asks his brother Vidura: how is a man to live with this? Vidura tells him a story. A man lost in a forest full of beasts runs and falls into a hidden well. He hangs head down, caught in creepers. Below is a great...
week 2.lesson: Life hangs by a thread that time is gnawing, and people forget it for a drop of honey; seeing this clearly is where freedom begins.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are asking what happens after death while holding the body of someone you loved. The man in the well also did not lose hope of living. Freedom begins when you see the thread and the drop at the same time.

week 3.verse line: We have come to you for shelter. Please make this fear, born of confusion, go away.
Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.
This tangle is hard to get through. Those who take shelter in me get through it.
Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.
Lead us by the good path. Keep crooked dealing far from us.
Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.

week 3.story: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
week 3.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
week 3.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

person.their note: I shouted at a junior in front of the whole team today over a small mistake. I saw his face. I can't take it back.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: You cannot take back the shouting, and the image of his face burns you now like the harsh words of kin that churn a fire stick.

week 1.verse line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
week 1.personal line written for them: You cannot take back the shouting, and the image of his face burns you now like the harsh words of kin that churn a fire stick.

week 1.verse line: In anger we lose the sense of what should never be said.
week 1.personal line written for them: You saw his face after you shouted. That image is a wound that will not close. You cannot take it back, but you can hold what you did without letting it become all of you.

week 1.verse line: Don't eat yourself up with shame for what someone else in your family did.
Free of craving, you stop replaying what you did and didn't do.
week 1.personal line written for them: You saw his face and you cannot take it back. The free one is done with what needed doing. He does not dwell on what he did or left undone.

week 1.verse line: Do today what lets you sleep tonight, and in youth what lets you rest in old age.
week 1.personal line written for them: You saw his face, and the weight of it will not lift until you choose differently. Do today what lets you sleep tonight, because in youth you are building the rest of your life.

week 1.verse line: Don't punish the whole world for one person's wrong.
week 1.personal line written for them: You saw the boy’s face. That pain is yours now. It does not have to be the end of the story.

week 1.story: Two exhausted brothers nearly destroy each other in a tent
week 1.summary: Yudhishthira lies wounded and humiliated; Karna beat him and let him live with a taunt. Arjuna leaves the fight to check on him. The elder brother assumes he has come with news that Karna is dead. He has not. Seventeen days of fear pour out: you have failed us, your bow is useless, give your...
week 1.lesson: Dharma is subtle, and a vow is not kept by an act that destroys what the vow was for.
week 1.personal line written for them: You saw his face. A vow to be a leader is not kept when it destroys the trust you were meant to protect. The moment is heavy with what cannot be taken back.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: I feel guilty about something I did

week 1.verse line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding the whole weight of this moment on your own shoulders, replaying it because you believe you alone caused the harm. You are one cause among the five, and that is your part to own. You are not the whole picture.

week 1.verse line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep going over what you did. You hold yourself to a standard you would never give a friend. That is the self striking the self. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy when it rehearses the same regret. You do not need to fix the past today.

week 1.verse line: Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding a standard that crushes you. The guilt is not a verdict on you. It is a sign that you care about doing right. What you did was not the end of your story. The effort you put in before still matters.

week 1.verse line: Free in that joy, one no longer agonises: 'Why didn't I do right? Why did I do wrong?'
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep going over it again and again, as if the loop itself could change the past. The weight of that is real. But the text asks what falls away for one who knows joy. Your work and your guilt are both real.

week 1.verse line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are replaying a moment at work, turning it over and over, as if you alone wrote the script and alone must carry the weight. The text asks you to stop treating your own mind as the enemy that must be punished.

week 1.verse line: Don't become bad because someone was bad to you. Stay good.
week 1.personal line written for them: The resentment you hold is a kind of wickedness turned inward, and it is exhausting you. You are not obligated to accept the wrong done to you, but you are free to stop letting it make you smaller. Choose to remain good in your own sight, for your own sake.

week 1.story: Six seekers wait a year
week 1.summary: Six earnest seekers come to the sage Pippalada with questions. Instead of answering, he asks them to live with him for a year in discipline and faith, and only promises to answer what he actually knows.
week 1.lesson: Readiness matters, and a good teacher only claims what he knows.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been waiting a long time to be told you are enough, but the truth is, you could sit with yourself first. The seekers who waited a year were not being tested. They were being prepared to hear the truth without running from it.

person.their note: I got promoted over two people with MBAs from top schools. I don't have one. I feel sick before every presentation, like they'll find out I don't belong.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: Your mind won't settle while you are working, and a verse was chosen with that weight in mind.

week 1.verse line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
week 1.personal line written for them: You feel sick before every presentation, as if they will find out you do not belong. This is the itch of envy, a disease of the mind that burns at another's happiness.

week 1.verse line: Learning is wealth no thief can see. It grows when you give it away and never perishes.
A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
week 1.personal line written for them: The water in your pot is the same whether it comes from a well or the ocean. Your worth does not shrink because you did not come from a top school. Stand steady and do not let the fear of being found out steal your dignity.

week 1.verse line: Want what is within reach. Enjoy what is here now. Don't grieve over what hasn't happened.
Not for any price. Some things are not for sale, however powerful the buyer.
week 1.personal line written for them: The promotion is a fortune you did not buy and cannot lose. Your place here is not a commodity traded for an MBA. You belong because you are here.

week 1.story: 'Sisters and Brothers of America': Chicago, 11 September 1893
week 1.summary: An unknown 30-year-old monk from India, with no invitation and little money, rises on the Parliament's opening day and greets the hall as 'Sisters and Brothers of America'. The audience stands and applauds for minutes. In a five-minute address he says India's faith accepts all religions as true...
week 1.lesson: You can belong fully to your own tradition and still honour every other path.
week 1.personal line written for them: The fear of not belonging is heavy, and it does not have to hold you back. You can step up while your mind is unsettled and your stomach is tight.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: I feel like an imposter

week 1.verse line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are sitting with the feeling of not being good enough after the promotion. You are holding yourself to a standard you would never give to a friend. The mind feels like a storm you cannot quiet. Still, the practice of letting go gives you a way to steady it.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 1.verse line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are sitting with the news that you were passed over while others moved ahead, and the voice telling you that you are not good enough is loud right now. Draupadi is saying that real prosperity does not grow from looking down on yourself.

week 1.verse line: Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.
week 1.personal line written for them: The promotion passed you by. Now your mind will not settle. You are waiting for the next test. Krishna says you are not ruined. The effort you put in is still there. You do not have to prove yourself all over again today. You pick up where you left off.

week 1.verse line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding yourself to a standard you would never put on a friend, and the mind is paying the price for it. The comparison and the sting of the passed-over promotion are real, but they are not the whole picture of who you are.

week 1.verse line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been waiting for someone to see you and fix how you feel, but no one is coming. You are the one who must choose to stop being your own worst critic.

week 1.verse line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been passed over and you keep comparing yourself to others, and the mind is restless because it is holding itself to a standard you would never give a friend. Vidula shows that a lost position is not a lost self.

week 1.story: Jambavant reminds Hanuman of his strength
week 1.summary: Nobody can leap the ocean. Old Jambavant admits honestly that he is no longer young. Then he turns to the silent Hanuman and asks why he sits quiet: what task in the world is too hard for him? Hanuman grows to the size of a mountain.
week 1.lesson: Sometimes we need someone else to remind us what we can do; and the old can be that someone.
week 1.personal line written for them: You sit in the meeting where the promotion goes to someone else, and the old doubt returns. It is not that you lack skill. It is that you have forgotten what you are capable of. Someone else once saw your strength when you could not see it yourself.

person.their note: I have two job offers and I have to decide by Friday. I change my mind every hour. Every time I pick one I feel I'm losing the other.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: You keep walking the same ground, and a verse is chosen to sit with you.

week 1.verse line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
week 1.personal line written for them: You feel you are losing the other offer every time you pick one. The mind is hard to hold, like the wind. Let the decision rest in the moment you are in.

week 1.verse line: Dullness, born of ignorance, ties you down through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.
week 1.personal line written for them: You feel you lose the other offer every time you choose, as if picking one is a kind of sleep that keeps you from seeing the path ahead.

week 1.verse line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are caught between two doors, and every step feels like a loss of the other. This path asks you to act without clinging to which door you open. Even a little of this steady action will shield you from that great fear.

week 1.verse line: If you think yourselves weak, weak you will be; if you think yourselves strong, strong you will be;
Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep going over the same two choices. Decide, then begin. Let the rest wait.

week 1.verse line: When your mind drifts to harmful things, steer it back to good ones. That's the whole teaching.

week 1.story: Hanuman's unease in Ravana's chambers
week 1.summary: Searching Ravana's palace at night, Hanuman finds himself looking across Ravana's sleeping wives and is seized by fear that he has broken dharma. He examines his own mind, finds it unmoved, reasons that the search itself required it, and goes on searching with a clear conscience.
week 1.lesson: Judge yourself by your intention and your mind's state, not only by what your eyes happened to meet while doing your duty.
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep going over the same choice. The mind behind it is not wrong; it is simply tired. Examine the necessity of the act honestly, then go on.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: I have to make a big decision

week 1.verse line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been turning the choice over and over because you think the wrong move will break you. The texts say that doing nothing is still a move. It just leaves you with the same question. The work in front of you is yours to do.

week 1.verse line: Anger clouds judgement, clouded judgement loses memory, lost memory wrecks reason, and then you fall.
week 1.personal line written for them: You keep going over the same decision again and again, as if you are stuck in a loop. The verse shows that the fall begins with what you dwell on. The choice itself is not the enemy.

week 1.verse line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
week 1.personal line written for them: The choice you keep turning over is heavy. But the path you are on is not a mistake. The noise of what might go wrong does not erase what you know is right.

week 1.verse line: Running away won't free you from pain. Free of clinging, you can be at peace right where you are.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are going over the same choice again and again. The idea here is that running away from your work or your fear will not end the ache. The peace you want is not a new place.

week 1.verse line: Never give up what is right, not for desire, not from fear, not for money.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are weighing your career against your fear of the unknown. Both paths feel like they ask something of you, and you have been carrying the choice alone. The right thing here is not a single job title.

week 1.verse line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing at a crossroads, thinking about a career change, and the weight of the decision is heavy. The texts call this torn between duties, and they say that the path you choose, even if it is not perfect, is the one that belongs to you.

week 1.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 1.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 1.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing where Janaka stood, hearing a different song and wondering if you could leave your job to find yourself. You do not have to run. You can walk into your work today with the same free mind Janaka chose. The choice is not between staying and leaving.

person.their note: I've worked 14-hour days for ten years. I have the house, the car, the title. And I feel completely empty. What was it all for?

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: You have the house, the car, the title, and still feel completely empty, so this mind of yours runs here and there for nothing like a stray village dog.

week 1.verse line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have the house and the title, yet the mind still runs far from them. The restlessness is not a failure of your effort. The wandering is simply what the mind does when it looks for something it has already lost.

week 1.verse line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have built the house and held the title, yet the river of wishing still runs. The water is full, but the banks of worry are high. You can rest on the bank today.

week 1.verse line: Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come.
week 1.personal line written for them: The house and the title are real. They are not the whole story. No good you have done is undone. The victory is sure to come.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 1.verse line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have worked fourteen-hour days for ten years. You have the house and the title, and the feeling remains. The absence of reward does not make the effort worthless.

week 1.verse line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have built the house and earned the title. Now the mind wanders through the rooms, finding them empty. Rest where you are. Let the day unfold without scripting it.

week 1.story: Sampati's burned wings
week 1.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's...
week 1.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.

week 2.verse line: I dug, sailed, flattered kings, chased every scheme, and gained not a broken coin. Enough, craving.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have the house, the car, and the title, yet the days still feel hollow. All that effort for a feeling of completion that never arrived. There is enough in this moment to stop chasing.

week 2.verse line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have worked hard for years and now the emptiness remains. The house and the title do not fill the space. The quiet truth is that the striving itself was the suffering all along.

week 2.verse line: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have built the house, the car, and the title through long days. The work is real, but the feeling of emptiness is also real. You can let the work continue while leaning on the grace that holds the lasting home.

week 2.verse line: There's no end to wanting. Contentment is the highest happiness, and the real wealth.
Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have the house, the car, the title. You have fed the days. Now let the house feed others. Let your roof become a world for the ones who pass through.

week 2.verse line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have built the house and the car, but the title feels hollow. The search is not over. There is still more ground to cover.

week 2.story: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
week 2.summary: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
week 2.lesson: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have the house, the car, and the title. And you feel completely empty. The last ten years were not for this.

week 3.verse line: What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?
week 3.personal line written for them: You have the house, the car, the title, and still the day ends in a hollow silence. The title and the house do not fill the space that remains. Rest in the question of who you are before the title.

week 3.verse line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have the title and the car. You also have the restless stirring that never stops. This is what rajas looks like in a life that is full of doing.

week 3.verse line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have the title, the house, the car. The outer life is full. The inner life is quiet. There is a joy in you that does not run out. It is already there.

week 3.verse line: Happiness is in the vast. There is no happiness in the small.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have the house and the title, but the small is not enough. The wanting is for the vast. Let that wanting be your guide today.

week 3.verse line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have built a house of facts, but the rooms feel hollow. The title and the car are just walls without a life inside them. You can still give or enjoy what you have, and that is where the meaning lives.

week 3.verse line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have the house and the title, but the work has hollowed you out. The sense of being the doer can fall away even while the days are long.

week 3.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
week 3.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

week 1.verse line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are in a season where the old reasons for moving have lost their pull, and the silence in your chest is asking what comes next. The work is there and the children are there, but the engine is quiet.

week 1.verse line: Same night, same day, the same tasks on repeat. We run in circles and call it living.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your work and your children fill the room, but the night comes the same way. The tasks repeat and you feel no shame. You are looking for what it is all for, and that search is the real work.

week 1.verse line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are in the middle of the same night, the same day, the same tasks on repeat. You run in circles and call it living. The texts say calm is not found by changing places or chasing it.

week 1.verse line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
week 1.personal line written for them: The same morning, the same drop-offs, the same work that asks for more. You are not failing. You are simply tired of the machine. The verse does not ask you to stop the work. It asks you to find a place inside that does not need to be fixed.

week 1.verse line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
week 1.personal line written for them: You do your work for the children and the family, but the weight of how it lands is too much to carry alone. Let the doing be enough for now. The work is yours, the rest is not.

week 1.verse line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are not sinking, but the same tasks on repeat have made the water feel heavy. Ribhu's way is not to escape the work but to move through it without the weight of wanting or not wanting.

week 1.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 1.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 1.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 1.personal line written for them: Janaka heard a song that shook him, yet he still answered his doorkeeper. Your work is full and your children need you, but the question you are carrying is real. You can do the day's work with a mind that does not clutch.

week 2.verse line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are in the middle of the week, looking at your own work and family, and the weight of it all has left you running on empty. You are not failing, you are simply tired of the old reasons that used to carry you.

week 2.verse line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are walking over a hidden treasure every day, and you do not know the spot. The weight of work and the children and the family pulls you outward, so you do not feel the ground beneath your feet.

week 2.verse line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are tired of running, yet the race is still on. Your past effort built the life you have, but it is also the weight pulling you down. This verse does not ask you to win the whole race today. It asks you to stay calm through the wrestling.

week 2.verse line: Knowing this, the wise stop arguing. Their joy is within, and they stay fully active.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are tired of the wrestling. Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling, and the exhaustion is real. But the joy that Angiras speaks of is not a reward for winning. It is a calm witness that sits beside you, already active in the background.

week 2.verse line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
week 2.personal line written for them: The work and the children and the family still need you, and they will not wait. But the meaning you are looking for is not in a new achievement or a quieter room. It is in how you meet the day.

week 2.verse line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have looked for meaning in big ideas, but the butcher says it is in the honest work you already do and the care you give your children and parents. You do not need to do more.

week 2.story: Bali tires of endless days and asks his father's riddle
week 2.summary: The demon king Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day at his window he realises he is doing the same things day after day, night after night, and asks what any of it adds up to. He remembers a riddle his father Virochana once told him: a vast realm ruled by a silent king and an...
week 2.lesson: When life feels like a loop, the work is not more of it but mastering the mind that runs it.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have done the conquering, the building, the showing up. Now you stand at the window and feel the loop. The children, the work, the family, they are not the problem. The mind is running the machine, and it is tired.

week 3.verse line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have been running on empty and asking what it is all for. The text says that the answer is not outside you. The one who watches the exhaustion, the children, the work, is the quiet witness already living inside you.

week 3.verse line: It is the very flavour of life. Whoever tastes it is filled with joy.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are looking for something deeper, and this is the pattern underneath it. The joy you are missing is not something you buy or achieve. It is the very flavour of life, waiting to be tasted. You are already filled with it.

week 3.verse line: Throne or begging bowl, gain or loss, crowd or solitude: a steady person stays the same.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have left the demands of work and the noise of the house to sit in the quiet of your own mind, yet the search for meaning still moves like a restless wind. The verse shows that peace is not a new place you reach.

week 3.verse line: Have faith, my child, have faith. You are more than everything that happens to you.
week 3.personal line written for them: The roles are heavy right now. The work, the children, the family. But you are not the roles. You are the space in which they happen. You are the quiet witness. The exhaustion is real, but it is a wave. You are the ocean.

week 3.verse line: Teach me how to keep working in the world without the work filling me with sorrow.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are looking for a deeper place to stand while the work is still there. The skill is not to do less, but to feel less owned by what you do. The children and the tasks are still yours, but they are not the whole of you.

week 3.verse line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are in the middle of your week, and the question from yesterday still sits in your chest. The work itself is not the enemy, but the way it fills you with sorrow is. You have laid your actions at the edge of the day.

week 3.summary: Bhrigu asks his father Varuna to teach him what is ultimate. Varuna gives only a clue and tells him to reflect. Bhrigu comes back four times with answers (food, breath, mind, understanding) and each time is sent back to go deeper, until he discovers that everything is born from joy, lives by joy...
week 3.lesson: A wise parent lets a child discover the answer instead of handing it over.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have asked what it is all for and found only empty rooms. The answer is not another task or achievement. It is a joy that was there before the roles and before the burnout. It is the ground beneath the work. You do not need to earn it.

week 1.personal line written for them: The good direction you see is not yours to hold alone. The credit belongs to the source that made it possible.

week 1.personal line written for them: You are building your own work while the ground beneath your feet is shifting. People watch what you do. Show up for the work that is in front of you. Let the rest wait.

week 1.verse line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building your own work while raising children and caring for your parents. It is a heavy load, and your mind is full. The teaching is that you are not the roles you play or the tasks you carry. You are the awareness that sees them all.

week 1.verse line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building your own work, raising children, and caring for your parents, all while studying. It is easy to think you could finish one thing before you begin another. But the days and nights are passing like arrows.

week 1.verse line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building something of your own while your days are full. The doubt you feel is using the energy that could start the work. Decide on one small step and begin it now, without waiting for the whole path to be clear.

week 1.story: Hanuman's leap

week 1.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building something that asks for your full weight, yet your mind keeps offering you places to pause. The texts say that steadiness and focus can walk together, and that knowing when to be large and when to be small is the mark of someone who will not sink.

week 1.story: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps

week 1.lesson: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
week 1.personal line written for them: The mind keeps circling the need to be liked. You do not have to earn the room you are already in.

week 1.verse line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.

week 1.verse line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are raising your children and watching them grow, and you are comparing your own path to the lives you see around you. The restlessness you feel comes from wanting the outcome to look a certain way before you allow yourself to rest.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 1.verse line: You ploughed and sowed. If the rain didn't come, that isn't your failure. Don't condemn yourself.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have done the sowing. The waiting is not a failure of yours. Your part is the work. The harvest is not the lock on your rest.

week 1.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are raising your children and your mind is restless because you could see a certain result before you let yourself rest. You can still do the work of the day and wish for a full life without letting the outcome hold you tight.

week 1.verse line: Results follow effort. Call it fate if you like, but it is the same effort.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing in the middle of your children's lives, looking back at your own choices and wondering if you ruined their future. The restlessness is the weight of thinking you could control the harvest.

week 1.personal line written for them: You are trying to hold the future together with your own hands, and it is exhausting. The verse does not ask you to stop caring. It asks you to loosen the grip. You are building your own thing, studying, and caring for your parents. You can do all of that.

week 1.verse line: Daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens.
week 1.personal line written for them: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

week 1.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 1.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 1.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 1.personal line written for them: Janaka stood on his roof and saw that his kingdom was still there, his duties were still there. Your work and your care for your parents are still there too. They do not need your mind to clutch them.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I feel lonely

week 1.verse line: Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are studying and feeling cut off, convinced you do not belong. This verse says that even the worst wrongdoer is carried across by the raft of knowledge. Let that be the truth of your desk right now. You do not need to be perfect to learn.

week 1.verse line: Where did this weakness come from, at the very moment it matters most?
week 1.personal line written for them: You are sitting in your own study space, feeling the weight of being unseen among your friends and doubting your place in your classes. This faintness is not a sign that you are failing.

week 1.verse line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are in the library or the hostel, and the distance between you and the friends you thought you had feels like a wide river you cannot cross. You feel unseen in the middle of the room.

week 1.verse line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
week 1.personal line written for them: The doubt and the loneliness you feel are not the whole truth. They are just weather passing through. There is a steadiness inside you that does not depend on anyone else seeing you. You can rest in that quiet place, even when the room feels empty.

week 1.verse line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been sitting with this feeling of being cut off, as if the space between you and your friends is a wall you built yourself. But the texts say that at your lowest, you do not need to fix the whole room.

week 1.verse line: See yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself, and you stop recoiling from people.
