week 1.personal line written for them: You feel cut off from the people around you. The Isha asks you to stop shrinking. If you can see your own face in theirs, the distance will not feel so hard to cross.

week 1.story: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
week 1.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning...
week 1.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
week 1.personal line written for them: Bhasa and Vilasa spent a lifetime proving their worth through effort, only to find themselves alone at the end. You are in a similar stretch, where the lists of what you could do to be enough keep spinning.

week 2.verse line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?
week 2.personal line written for them: You are in a room with people but you feel like the only one there. The distance between you and your friends is real, even if no one has said a word. You are not wrong to feel this way. The fear is not a weakness.

week 2.reference: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
week 2.verse line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
week 2.personal line written for them: That unease in the study hall, the silence between texts, is the mind spinning. You are not cut off, but the mind is making a room where no one is. The people still in front of you are your next step.

week 2.verse line: Good or bad, we are still yours.
week 2.personal line written for them: The quiet in the library and the doubt that you do not belong are heavy. You do not have to carry the weight of being worthy alone. There is a belonging that is already given, not earned. Let that be the ground you stand on.

week 2.verse line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have been trying to explain your loneliness to your friends as if it is a problem they can fix. But the feeling of being cut off does not need to be translated for them. The distance you feel is not a failure of communication.

week 2.verse line: Even one meeting with a good person is a gift. Time with good people is never wasted.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have been waiting for the others to notice you, to close the distance. But the distance is not just theirs. It grows because you are not yet among the good you wish to be. You are in the study, but you are not yet with the good.

week 2.verse line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have felt cut off from the friends around you. The distance grew quietly. Now you sit with your books and feel like an imposter. But the self is the only friend you can truly count on in this room.

week 2.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
week 2.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have been sitting with this feeling of being an imposter and feeling cut off from your friends. Sita was surrounded by people who mocked her and kept her lonely. She worried Ram had forgotten her. But she held on to the truth that real love survives distance.

week 3.verse line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are studying in a room full of people, yet you feel like an imposter because you believe you could earn the right to be there. This verse says you do not have to earn it.

week 3.verse line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
week 3.personal line written for them: The doubt you carry about your place in the room is a belief, not a fact. This week has started to show you that your worth is not earned by a test score or a friend's text.

week 3.verse line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are sitting in your study, looking at your friends, and you feel the distance between you. You think they see something you do not have, and that thought is the stain. But the self is the same sky in them that it is in you.

week 3.verse line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are sitting in the library or your room, and the feeling of being an imposter is loud. The verse tells you that the part of you that notices this feeling is the same quiet witness that is in everyone. It is not judging.

week 3.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are studying and feeling cut off, as if the people around you are moving through a room you are not in. The verse says to do your work and wish for a hundred years, not to stop trying, but to do it without letting it own you.

week 3.verse line: You never once delayed. You are easy to reach, and remembering you is enough to win you.
week 3.personal line written for them: The distance you feel is not because anyone turned away, but because you are waiting for a sign that never arrives. The texts say that the Lord is already easy to reach. You do not need to prove your worth to be seen.

week 3.story: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
week 3.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.
week 3.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.
week 3.personal line written for them: In your own place of study, a friend offered a quiet truth. That is what you need right now. The silence between you is not a wall, but a space waiting for a single honest word. Let the knowing come first, before the knowing becomes a burden you carry alone.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: You feel like you'll never be loved without being abandoned, and the harsh words of your own kin keep churning your heart like a fire stick.

week 1.verse line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
week 1.personal line written for them: You carry the sting of words that should have been safe. Even Krishna felt his own kin churn his heart like a fire-stick. Let this be the truth you hold today: you are allowed to feel the burn.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
week 1.verse line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
week 1.personal line written for them: Something someone did stays with you. The mind then spins around that hurt, adding pain to the wound. You can notice when the mind is wandering, and let the first hurt be just what it is.

week 1.verse line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
week 1.personal line written for them: Something someone did stays with you, and you feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. Rightness is the only power that does not leave, and truth is its name. Stand in that truth today.

week 1.verse line: Your wisdom isn't gone. Grief has only put it to sleep for a while.
week 1.personal line written for them: Someone left a mark on you that still hurts. That pain is not the end of your story. Your own clear mind is waiting for you to return to it.

week 1.verse line: The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.
week 1.personal line written for them: You feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. That pain is real. Strength lives in you even now.

week 1.verse line: Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and self-respect, and know the power in you.
week 1.personal line written for them: Something someone did stays with you. You feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and know the power that is already in you.

week 1.story: Karna comes alone to the man who insulted him
week 1.summary: For years the old commander belittled him in open court, and Karna swore not to fight while Bhishma led. Now Bhishma lies on the arrows, the crowd has gone, and Karna comes in the dark, falls at his feet and says, his voice breaking: I am Radha's son, the one you always looked at with dislike.
week 1.lesson: A harsh word can come from concern, and an old quarrel can be ended at a deathbed without either side giving up what he stands for.
week 1.personal line written for them: The words that hurt you still sit in your chest. They do not have to be the final word. You can carry them without letting them define you.

week 2.verse line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.
week 2.personal line written for them: Something someone did stays with you, and you feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. That pain is a weight you carry, but it is not the whole of you.

week 2.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 2.verse line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
If they were truly wicked, would they have turned toward me at all?
week 2.personal line written for them: Something someone did stays with you. You do not need to be wicked in heart to have turned toward love. The one who comes to the door is already counted.

week 2.verse line: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
week 2.personal line written for them: The hurt of being abandoned can feel like proof you are not lovable. But this verse says you are the one with the power to lift yourself. You can be your own steady friend today.

week 2.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.
week 2.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.
week 2.personal line written for them: You feel you will only be loved if you are abandoned. The waiting has turned into self-blame. You do not need to look at your own record right now.

week 3.verse line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
week 3.personal line written for them: You know the words that are supposed to help, and you still feel the weight of what was done. Understanding does not lift the hurt. Let the ache be where it is for now, without asking it to leave.

week 3.verse line: Whatever you start calling 'mine' becomes a source of pain the day you lose it.
week 3.personal line written for them: You feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. The grip on that hope is what hurts. Let it go.

week 3.verse line: That subtle essence is the self of all that is. That is truth. You are that, Shvetaketu.
week 3.personal line written for them: You feel you will never be loved without being abandoned, and something stays with you. The verse says the subtle essence is the self of all that is. You are not small.

week 3.verse line: Caste is not in skin, blood, flesh or bone. The self has no caste; caste is a social convention.
week 3.personal line written for them: A label fixed at birth has no hold on what you are. You are not that hurt, and you are not that label.

week 3.verse line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are studying and feeling that old hurt still lives inside you. A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times. Let this be your measure for how you might let yourself be held.

week 3.verse line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
week 3.personal line written for them: The hurt you carry is real and heavy. You do not have to hold it alone. Stay close to those who steady you today.

week 3.story: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps
week 3.summary: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango...
week 3.lesson: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
week 3.personal line written for them: The hurt of being left is still with you, and that is real. You do not have to earn care by being perfect. One honest asking is enough to be met.

person.their note: My mother started chemo last month. I run between the hospital, the office and home alone. At 3am I google survival rates.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

week 1.verse line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are carrying the weight of how things will turn out before they even arrive. You are trying to control the result to make the waiting feel safe. Let the work in front of you have its own value, separate from the future it might bring.

week 1.verse line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are carrying the weight of the outcome, not just the work. That is where the exhaustion lives. Let the work be what it is, and let your mind rest from the result.

week 1.verse line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
week 1.personal line written for them: The work at hand is yours, the outcome is not. Let the next task be enough. You are busy on the outside and unhurried inside. The work at hand is enough.

week 1.verse line: A ball knocked down bounces back up. For good people, setbacks rarely last.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are carrying the weight of how things will turn out, and that is what keeps you running on empty. The verse places its trust in the path you are already on, not in a perfect result. Your work is yours to do. The results are not yours to hold.

week 1.verse line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are carrying the weight of how the day turns out for your parents and your work. The Gita says peace comes when you let go of that grip. The rest is not indifference.

week 1.verse line: Results follow effort. Call it fate if you like, but it is the same effort.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding the future like a weight in your hands, waiting for the work to turn out a certain way before you will rest. The tiredness is not just the care. It is the refusal to let the effort be enough. Today, let the work be the work.

week 1.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 1.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 1.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are doing the work of the day and caring for your parents while your mind is still caught in the question of how it will all turn out. Janaka did not leave his kingdom to find peace.

week 2.verse line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
week 2.personal line written for them: The tiredness you feel comes from the mind running through every task and outcome. It is not the work itself that drains you, but the endless list of what must happen before you can stop. Let the mind rest in the doing, not only in the results.

week 2.verse line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is restless because it is chained to how things must turn out before you can rest. This is the pattern underneath your exhaustion. Let the work be what it is without letting the result decide your peace. The work is yours, not the outcome.

week 2.verse line: Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.
week 2.personal line written for them: The lists in your head are endless because you are holding the outcome. The work at your desk and the care at the hospital both ask for your full skill, but the result belongs to the moment, not to your mind. You do what you can do.

week 2.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 2.verse line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your part is the effort, not the outcome; work done well is already complete, whatever result comes.

week 2.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 2.personal line written for them: The lists for work and for your parents never seem to end, and the mind stays restless because it wants the results to land a certain way before it can rest.

week 2.verse line: Do not drift from truth or duty. Do not neglect your wellbeing, your prosperity, or your learning.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are standing at a point where the work and the care for your parents pull in different directions. The mind wants to settle on a single outcome, but the days keep moving. This verse asks you to hold the work and the care as part of one whole life.

week 2.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.
week 2.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
week 2.personal line written for them: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

week 3.verse line: The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind is caught in the coming and going of days, of work, of worry. You feel the weight of what might happen next. But you are not the one who must hold it all. You are the space in which these worries move, not the worries themselves.

week 3.verse line: Teach me how to keep working in the world without the work filling me with sorrow.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your part is the effort, not the outcome; work done well is already complete, whatever result comes.

week 3.verse line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind will not settle because you are trying to hold the outcome before it happens. The teaching is to do the work and let the result go, to be steady in success and failure. You are not the work. You are the one who stands apart from it.

week 3.verse line: Throne or begging bowl, gain or loss, crowd or solitude: a steady person stays the same.
week 3.personal line written for them: The work and the care for your parents are your throne and your forest. You do not need to run from one to the other to find rest. The same mind that holds the work can hold the care. The same breath can move through both.

week 3.verse line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.
week 3.personal line written for them: The body comes and goes. What you truly are does not. Praised, don't gloat. Blamed, don't curse others.

week 3.verse line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
week 3.personal line written for them: The work with your parents and your job demands your full attention, but the result is not yours to own. The rest you need comes from letting go of the outcome. Your part is the effort, not the final shape of things.

week 3.story: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
week 3.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
week 3.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
week 3.personal line written for them: Pingala waited for a man who would never come, and her peace was stolen by the waiting. Your mind is doing the same thing with the future, holding on to how the work and the care must turn out. The exhaustion is the cost of that waiting.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: Your mind won't settle between the hospital, the office, and home at 3am, so this verse speaks to the end of the one who tries and slips.

week 1.verse line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind circles the hospital at three in the morning. The faith that brought you here is real, and your effort is seen even when it feels too small to hold.

week 1.verse line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
week 1.personal line written for them: At three in the morning, your mind spins through every possibility. This world of worry is built by your own thinking, and you can stop adding to it.

week 1.verse line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind runs between the hospital and the office. That fever of what happened and what will come keeps you awake. You can let it go, and still keep moving.

week 1.verse line: I bow to you, Goddess: you end great fear, you ease great hardship, you are compassion itself.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind circles the survival rates at three in the morning. The Goddess is the compassion that meets you in this hard place. Let her form hold you while you wait.

week 1.verse line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
week 1.personal line written for them: You run between the hospital, the office, and home alone. Your mind is shaken, and you search for answers in the dark. The fear is there, but you do not have to let it choose for you.

week 1.story: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
week 1.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow...
week 1.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
week 1.personal line written for them: You move between the hospital, the office, and home alone. Your mind will not settle. The breath is a place to rest that is always available to you.

week 2.verse line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is carrying your understanding away from the shore. The hospital, the office, and the search at three in the morning are the wind. You are the boat, and your wisdom is being swept off course. Notice where the wind is taking you.

week 2.verse line: A child relies on its mother and stops worrying; she has to look after it.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is running between the hospital, the office and home alone. The worry is heavy. A child relies on its mother and stops worrying, because she has to look after it.

week 2.verse line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is moving between the hospital and the office at three in the morning. The present moment is where you are already standing. It is enough to meet it as it is.

week 2.verse line: Freedom has four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. Win one, and the others follow.
Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your mind is caught in the hospital corridors and the office and the dark hours of the morning. The past has already happened, and the future has not yet arrived. Rest in the exact moment you are in right now.

week 2.story: Kabir to his own restless mind: slowly, slowly
week 2.summary: The mind wants the result now. Kabir talks to it the way a gardener would.
week 2.lesson: Water faithfully; the fruit comes in its season, not because you poured more.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are giving everything to the hospital, the office, and the house. The fruit of this care will come in its own season. The timing is not in your hands.

week 3.verse line: The mind is faster than the wind, and worries outnumber the blades of grass.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind outruns the wind while you run between the hospital, the office, and home. The worries outnumber the blades of grass you pass on the way. Let the mind be fast for a moment. Let the worries be many. You are not asked to stop them today.

week 3.verse line: Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind is being pulled by the turbulence of the moment. The effort to care and to work is real, and the senses carry the mind even here.

week 3.verse line: Two birds, close friends, sit on one tree. One eats the sweet fruit; the other just watches.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind is busy tasting the bitter fruit of the night. There is also a quiet companion on the branch, simply watching, not shaken by the taste.

week 3.verse line: Don't chase your pleasures and pains. Know the one who feels them.
An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
week 3.personal line written for them: You move between hospital, office, and home. The worry circles at 3am because the mind is looking for an answer it cannot hold. Rest comes when the hand is busy with one thing, not when the mind searches for certainty.

week 3.verse line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
week 3.personal line written for them: The running between the hospital and the office leaves no room for rest. You can still turn inward while you do all of it.

week 3.story: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
week 3.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
week 3.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your mind keeps swinging between the hospital and the office. Patient return and clear inquiry into what you are is the way through this. You can rest in that stillness.

person.their note: At 58 I am starting my own company. Everyone says it is late. I feel hopeful and I want to keep this energy.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I've retired and feel lost

week 1.verse line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have chosen your own path after a long life of work. The comparison to others is a habit of the mind, not a measure of your worth. You are free to do your own work, flaws and all, simply because it is yours.

week 1.verse line: A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building your own thing, and the comparison to others is the fog that clouds your resolve. The texts say that resolve is the raw material of your life. When you compare, you borrow their blueprint instead of laying your own foundation.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 1.verse line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building something of your own after a lifetime of other people's demands. That work is yours now, even when the path is unclear. The comparison you feel is a sign that you are still looking outward for a finish line that does not exist.

week 1.verse line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have built your own work, and now the morning asks what comes next without a title or a deadline. The comparison with others is a ghost. Your resolve is the only measure. You are becoming what you choose to resolve.

week 1.verse line: Don't announce your plans; let people see your results.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have stepped away from a life of announcements and are now making something quiet. The comparison you feel is the noise of others' plans. Let your own work show what it is before you speak of it. The results are yours alone.

week 1.verse line: Get up and do today's work. Great people don't let the hour slip by.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have decided to build something of your own, and that is a true resolve. The test is not the decision but the morning when the work stops feeling exciting. You do not have to leave your life to change it.

week 1.story: Hanuman's leap
week 1.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
week 1.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building what belongs to you, and the work itself is the test. There will be moments when the path feels endless, when you compare your quiet progress to the noise of others, but the path is yours to walk. The mountain will rise.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: You want to keep this energy going at fifty-eight, and this verse says such calm learning and free wandering are the fruit of great austerity.

week 1.verse line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building something new at this stage of life. The freedom you have now, the simple food you eat, and the calm learning you are doing are the fruit of great austerity. Keep this energy going.

week 1.verse line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
Moderate in food and rest, in work and play, in sleep and waking: that's how sorrow eases.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are building something new. Keep your food, sleep, and play measured so this energy can last.

week 1.verse line: Duty is sweet only through love, and love shines in freedom alone.
week 1.personal line written for them: The energy you feel is the love greasing the wheels. Let this new company be the freedom where your duty becomes sweet.

week 1.verse line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
In bad times, good siblings are the hands that rise to block the blow.

week 1.story: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
week 1.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.
week 1.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have grown what was given to you, and now you return it to its source with nothing held back. That completion is the work itself.

person.their note: I am retired and when I look back I am grateful for how life has turned out. I want to keep this feeling.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I've retired and feel lost

week 1.verse line: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.
week 1.personal line written for them: The map you used to follow has run out, and now you are standing in a quiet room with no instructions. You do not need to build a new temple to find meaning.

week 1.verse line: Starving, a handful of grain is everything. Full, the whole earth looks like straw.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your days now hold more than enough, yet the old habit of needing a grand purpose still makes the room feel hollow. The value you once gave to a title or a project has shifted. What looks like straw to you now is the quiet ground beneath your feet.

week 1.verse line: Every pleasure leaves someday. Released freely, it brings peace; torn away, it brings torment.
week 1.personal line written for them: Turn inward, come to know the self, and let your work become service and offering; a life lived from there is full.

week 1.verse line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have spent a lifetime building a life that is now complete. You are walking over the one thing you were looking for without knowing it. The treasure is not a new project or a new role. It is the self that has always been here.

week 1.verse line: Put the effort you spend earning money into growing wiser first.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have spent a lifetime earning what the world calls success. Now the gold is here and the search is over. You can still tend to your days, but let the old clutch go. Let the morning paper or the evening walk be enough without proving anything.

week 1.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are in a time when the old reasons for working have faded, yet the days still ask for your attention. This verse does not ask you to do more, but to do what remains with a lighter hand.

week 1.story: Satyakama Jabala, the honest boy
week 1.summary: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having...
week 1.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.
week 1.personal line written for them: You stand at the edge of a new chapter, not because a door closed, but because the map you carried no longer points to a destination. The search for what it is all for is not a failure of the last forty years.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: You want to keep this gratitude, and the best gain is health, the highest happiness is contentment.

week 1.verse line: The best gain is health. The highest happiness is contentment.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have reached a place where what you have is enough. This quiet satisfaction is a form of wealth. Let it sit with you today.

week 1.verse line: As your desire, so your will; as your will, so your deeds; as your deeds, so you become.
week 1.personal line written for them: You chose to hold onto this gratitude. It is a quiet proof of how your own desire shaped the life you built. Let it remain a steady light today.

week 1.verse line: Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have reached a good place where life feels full, and that fullness has a shape. It is a quiet gratitude that rests on the years of giving and receiving. Hold on to this feeling, and let it remind you that the highest good is found in this mutual flow.

week 1.verse line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your gratitude for how life has turned out is a quiet form of action. You can let this feeling guide what you do next, even in small ways for others.

week 1.verse line: Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.
He thanked the mountain and said: how can I rest before Ram's work is done?
week 1.personal line written for them: You are grateful for the life you have built. This feeling is a gift, yet your spirit knows it is not meant to be held still. Let it move you into the work that still waits.

week 1.story: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
week 1.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.
week 1.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have grown what was given to you, and now you return it without claim. This quiet completion is your life's purpose fulfilled.

person.their note: My in-laws belittle me in front of guests and make me do all the work at home after my office job. My husband stays silent.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: Tension with my in-laws

week 1.verse line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
week 1.personal line written for them: The picture you hold of how things should be keeps breaking, and that hurts. The mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Practice and letting go can train it. Let the picture break.

week 1.verse line: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow. You live out the fruit of your own actions.
week 1.personal line written for them: The blame you hold for your in-laws and the fights with your partner is a chain of causes you are also in. You cannot hand your peace to them. Let your own part in the pattern be seen. The picture of how they were meant to be is what breaks.

week 1.verse line: 'Ours' and 'theirs' is how small minds count. For the large-hearted, the whole earth is family.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding the line between your family and your in-laws. The verse asks you to treat the whole earth as family. That does not mean you could agree with everyone.

week 1.verse line: No grudges, no quarrels, no craving, no fear: for such a person every direction is joy.
week 1.personal line written for them: The mind grows stormy when it holds on to what should be different. You feel the weight of your in-laws' words and your partner's silence. That picture you hold of how things should be is what breaks. You are skilled and wise enough to see the storm without fighting it.

week 1.verse line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
week 1.personal line written for them: The mind is a storm between what your in-laws did and the picture you hold of how they were meant to be. That picture is breaking, and it hurts. The way forward is not to win the argument or wait for them to change.

week 1.verse line: Turn no one away from your door. Make that a vow, and keep enough to share.
week 1.personal line written for them: The fights with your in-laws and the tension at home are eating at you. You are trying to hold on to the picture of a perfect family. This verse asks you to stop guarding the table and start gathering enough for everyone. You do not need to fix them.

week 1.story: Sumitra sits with Kausalya
week 1.summary: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.
week 1.lesson: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.
week 1.personal line written for them: The picture you hold of how your family should be keeps breaking, and that hurts. Sumitra did not tell Kausalya to stop grieving. She sat with her in the ache. You do not need to fix the picture right now.

week 2.verse line: Bear with me as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
week 2.personal line written for them: The tension with your in-laws and the fights with your partner come from an expectation that they should be different from who they are. You have been holding a picture of how you were meant to be, and it keeps breaking.

week 2.verse line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
week 2.personal line written for them: The fight with your partner and the unease with your in-laws are heavy enough on their own.

week 2.verse line: Everyone, gentle or fierce, comes to trust a calm person, the way we trust a mother.
week 2.personal line written for them: The fighting with your partner and the tension with your in-laws are loud because your mind is restless. A calm presence is not about being quiet. It is about the steadiness you hold inside the room. Trust is not demanded. It is offered by the calm you carry.

week 2.verse line: Praised by the good or harassed by the cruel, the free person stays the same.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are caught between two rooms, the one with your in-laws and the one with your partner, and the expectation of how each should be has cracked. The picture of a calm home is breaking against the noise. The free person is not the one who stops the noise.

week 2.verse line: Cut craving, forgive, drop arrogance, speak truth, win over even enemies, be kind to those suffering.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are trying to win over your in-laws, but you are also holding on to how they should be. You are waiting for them to change their nature. That waiting is a craving.

week 2.verse line: Understand quickly, listen long, act from judgement not impulse, and stay out of others' business unless asked.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are caught between the fight with your partner and the tension with your in-laws, and you are trying to manage both. Vidura says the wise person does not meddle in other people's affairs unasked.

week 2.story: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
week 2.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning...
week 2.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are standing in the same place, having done the hard work of building a life, yet the mind never stops. The endless lists of what you have done and what you could do keep you from the quiet you need.

week 3.verse line: You are not your body or your achievements. You are the awareness watching it all. Live lightly.
week 3.personal line written for them: The picture you hold of how your in-laws or partner should be is a wave crashing against the shore of your mind. The fight with your partner and the tension with your in-laws are not the real you. You are the awareness that sees the storm.

week 3.verse line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are caught between your in-laws and your partner. The anger you feel comes from dwelling on what they did or what they should be. That constant replay turns into wanting them to change, and when they do not, the frustration hardens into a fight.

week 3.verse line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are in a room with people who do not meet your picture of them, and you feel the stain of their actions on you. Krishna says the self is the sky, untouched by the clouds.

week 3.verse line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
week 3.personal line written for them: You keep fighting with your partner because you are trying to get them to be different. The fight is the loss, the quiet is the gain. Your mind is full of what is missing. Let the fight be there without letting it fill you.

week 3.verse line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your in-laws and partner are not keeping score of you. The picture you hold of how they were meant to be is breaking because you are measuring their actions against an idea of them that does not exist.

week 3.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 3.personal line written for them: The fighting with your partner and the unease with your in-laws come from holding on to how things should be. The verse asks you to keep doing what you do, but to let go of the grip. Your part is the work, not the result.

week 3.summary: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.
week 3.lesson: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are standing in a version of the morning Ram left, where your own leaving feels like a betrayal. You want to hold your partner close, yet your in-laws stand in the doorway, and the fight with them is the fight with the person you love.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: Someone else's actions have left a mark on your days, and a verse was chosen with that in mind.

week 1.verse line: I swallowed insults and forced laughter with an empty heart. Hope, how much longer will you make me dance?
week 1.personal line written for them: You have swallowed the belittling words and forced laughter so the house would run. That empty performance took everything. You do not need to keep dancing for them.

week 1.reference: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
week 1.verse line: When wrong crushes right while others watch in silence, the silent are wounded too.
Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
week 1.personal line written for them: The disrespect you face is not a measure of your worth. Right is a power that stands above every loud voice and silent witness.

week 1.verse line: Whoever runs others down in public only puts their own faults on display.
week 1.personal line written for them: When they belittle you in front of others, they are only showing their own smallness. Their silence about your hard work after your office day tells its own story. You carry the truth of your worth, not theirs.

week 1.verse line: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
week 1.personal line written for them: You do not have to shrink to the shape of the room. You absorb what is good, and you grow into your own tree. Your worth is not theirs to measure.

week 1.verse line: Some clouds bring rain, some only thunder. Don't plead with everyone you meet.
week 1.personal line written for them: You do not need to plead for respect in a room that already has it. The silence you are owed is your own. Let the thunder pass without asking it to stay.

week 1.story: A boy bent in eight places walks into the king's court, and the court laughs
week 1.summary: Ashtavakra was born with his body bent in eight places. As a boy of about twelve he learns that his father lost a debate at King Janaka's court to the scholar Bandi and was made to pay with his life. He walks to the palace. The gatekeeper will not let a child in.
week 1.lesson: A person is to be measured by what they know and are, not by age or body.

week 2.verse line: Why blame me, who knew nothing? You know what I feel for him.
week 2.personal line written for them: Someone you love has accused you of a wrong you did not commit. Your silence is not guilt. You know the truth of your own heart, and that is enough.

week 2.verse line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.

week 2.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 2.verse line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.

week 2.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 2.verse line: Force isn't always right, and forgiveness isn't always right. Wisdom is knowing which the moment needs.
week 2.personal line written for them: You carry the weight of a silent room. The moment does not always ask for quiet, and it does not always ask for force. It asks for a clear eye.

week 2.verse line: anything that makes you weak physically, intellectually, and spiritually, reject as poison;
week 2.personal line written for them: The belittling and silence you carry is poison. It weakens you. Reject it. Truth is strengthening. Keep this in mind today.

week 2.verse line: You may visit family without an invitation. But where there is hostility toward you, going brings no good.
week 2.personal line written for them: You come home from your office job and face the work they expect. You do not have to walk into a room where you are belittled. Your worth is not reduced by their contempt.

week 2.summary: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.
week 2.lesson: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.
week 2.personal line written for them: The doubt they cast is not yours to carry. Your own steady word and quiet conduct are already clearing you, one person at a time.

week 3.verse line: Flatterers are easy to find. Rare is the one who tells the hard truth, rarer the one who hears it.
week 3.personal line written for them: The people around you offer easy praise, not hard counsel. Your own voice is the rare one that speaks what is unwelcome but good.

week 3.verse line: Change not thy nature, gentle bloom, Thou violet, sweet and pure, But ever pour thy sweet perfume Unasked, unstinted, sure!
week 3.personal line written for them: Your gentle nature is not a weakness others can take from you. You keep your own worth, even when the room is full of noise.

week 3.verse line: Turn a torch upside down and its flame still rises. Steadiness survives humiliation.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your steadiness is not theirs to take. It remains upright even when the world inverts it.

week 3.verse line: Whether a careless person praises or blames you, what can it do? It's a crow cawing in the forest.
week 3.personal line written for them: Their words are just noise. You are not diminished by the cawing. Your worth is not up for their vote.

week 3.verse line: Make your children strong from their very childhood;
week 3.personal line written for them: The words spoken in your home are not the measure of your worth. You carry the strength of your own soul, and that cannot be taken away by silence or by belittlement.

week 3.verse line: People walk over the soft and fear the harsh. Be firm when it's needed, gentle when it's needed.
week 3.personal line written for them: The room does not get smaller because they say so. You carry the strength of the office into the evening. You do not need to be harsh to be firm.

week 3.story: Karna is asked for his lineage and has no answer
week 3.summary: Karna walks into the royal arena uninvited and matches every feat Arjuna has just performed. He challenges him to single combat. Then Kripa asks him to announce his mother, father and royal house, because princes do not duel men of unknown family. Karna's face falls like a lotus beaten down by rain.
week 3.lesson: A person shut out for his birth will give everything to the one who first treats him as an equal.

person.their note: Got the offer letter last week after eight months of looking. Things are finally turning and I want to keep it going.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: Everything in my life is changing at once

week 1.verse line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing at a crossroads where everything is shifting at once, and the fear of how it will turn out is making the next step feel impossible. The work in front of you is yours to do, and the result is not yours to hold.

week 1.verse line: Don't turn a sure thing into a gamble. Do the certain part first.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing at a crossroads, and every path looks like a gamble. You want to choose the sure thing, the one step that will not lose what you have found. Let your first move be the one that builds trust, not the one that proves a point.

week 1.verse line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your work is yours to do. The results are not yours to hold. Let the noise of what comes next stay outside your door. The path is clear right now. Take the next step and keep going.

week 1.verse line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are facing a lot of change at once and wondering if you could stay in your job or leave. The energy is there but it is caught in doubt. This verse suggests that the steadiness you need is not found in a new title or a different door.

week 1.verse line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing at the edge of a big change and the waiting is eating your time. The doubt you feel is not a sign to pause. It is the cost of moving. Do the one thing you are sure of right now, and let the rest wait its turn.

week 1.verse line: The rains are here. Wait for autumn. Some seasons are for waiting, not fighting.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are in a season of waiting too. The roads are closed. Do not turn a sure thing into a gamble by rushing into a change you cannot control. Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.

week 1.story: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
week 1.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind...
week 1.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are standing at a crossroads with everything shifting at once. King Janaka heard a truth that shook him to the core, yet he did not flee his kingdom. He returned to his duties with a mind that no longer clung to outcomes.

week 2.verse line: When 'I still have to do this' burns you up inside, only a rain of calm brings relief.
week 2.personal line written for them: The pressure to manage every change at once is the blazing sun inside you. You are trying to secure the future before it arrives. Calm is not the absence of change. It is the cooling rain on the roof of your ordinary day, right where you are.

week 2.verse line: The good and the pleasant both knock. The wise choose the good; the foolish grab the pleasant.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are standing at a moment where many doors are opening at once, and each one promises a different kind of relief. The pleasant ones promise an easy exit, a quick win, or a way to stop feeling anxious.

week 2.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
week 2.verse line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are watching everything change at once. Do right for its own sake, then work as if the outcome depends entirely on you.

week 2.verse line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are facing a season where everything is shifting at once, and the question of staying or leaving is heavy. The teaching says that the part of you which is steady does not need to stop the storm. It only needs to remain even while the storm passes.

week 2.verse line: Act at the right time, do what the task needs, and don't cling. That is a great doer.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your life is changing at once and you are anxious about how it will turn out. This is the text's stuck and not starting.

week 2.verse line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
week 2.personal line written for them: You are standing at the edge of a change you chose, but doubt is making the starting line feel like a wall. The texts say doing nothing is still a choice, and that choice is costing you the energy you could move.

week 2.summary: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.
week 2.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have set everything in motion, and now you are waiting to see what lands. You can rest in this pause without letting the doubt eat the ground you have already tilled. Let the waiting be a season, not a surrender.

week 3.verse line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are standing at a crossroads where everything is shifting, and the mind is telling you that you could choose the right path to be safe. Ashtavakra says the choice itself is not the problem. You are the awareness that watches the choices, not the choices themselves.

week 3.verse line: The mind alone binds or frees us: hooked on things, it binds; free of them, it liberates.
week 3.personal line written for them: No effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

week 3.verse line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are standing at a point where everything is shifting at once, and your body feels the weight of every choice. But the part of you that is watching this change is not the thing that is changing. It is the sky, and it is clean.

week 3.verse line: While we are still here, let us know it. Not knowing it is the great loss.
week 3.personal line written for them: All these changes are pulling you in every direction at once, and you are trying to decide what comes next before you have even settled into the next room. The texts say you become what you do.

week 3.verse line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are in the middle of a big shift and the question of staying or leaving is still open. That is exactly where Vidura's wise person stands. They decide, then begin. Their mind is not scattered by the change. They keep themselves in hand, steady through the uncertainty.

week 3.verse line: Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.
week 3.personal line written for them: You are standing at a fork in your career, and the weight of the outcome is keeping you still. The skill is not in choosing the perfect path right now. It is in taking the next step with your full attention. Let the result go.

week 3.summary: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has...
week 3.lesson: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.
week 3.personal line written for them: Vibhishan left a place that was not safe and crossed a wide sea to find Ram. Ram did not wait to see what Vibhishan could give him. He opened his arms because the heart that crossed was clean. You are standing at your own edge right now.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: You want to keep this good momentum going, and the steady do not step off the right path.

week 1.verse line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have the offer in hand and the energy to keep it going. Let the praise and the noise around you pass. Hold to the path that brought you here today.

week 1.verse line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are the kind of doer who moves forward without boasting. Your steadiness and energy are already here. Let this resolve be your quiet ground today.

week 1.verse line: Watch a man do his most common actions; those are indeed the things which will tell you the real character of a great man.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been waiting for this turn. What matters now is the steady, ordinary work you do each day. Let your new role be a place to show up with calm, steady action.

week 1.verse line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
week 1.personal line written for them: You decided, and now the offer is here. Keep the same steady hand you used to find it, and let the work begin without looking back.

week 1.verse line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.

week 1.story: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
week 1.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
week 1.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

week 2.verse line: May the good you have lived by, gladly and faithfully, now protect you.
In anger we lose the sense of what should never be said.
Unshaken in sorrow, not craving in joy, free of clinging, fear and anger: that is a steady mind.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have turned a corner, and now you want to stay there. A steady mind does not mean no feeling. It means feeling without being run by it. Let your new work be a place to practice that.

week 2.verse line: Take in big joys and big sorrows the way the ocean takes in rivers: evenly.
week 2.personal line written for them: The offer is a river flowing into you. Let it in, and let anything else in, the same way.

week 2.verse line: Steadiness comes from doing. No one becomes steady without acting; act, and steadiness follows.
week 2.personal line written for them: Your offer letter is the doing that steadies you. Let this action hold you. The work itself is the path.

week 2.verse line: Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.

week 2.story: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
week 2.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.
week 2.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
week 2.personal line written for them: You have let pride step aside to reach your king. The offer letter is your court, and your quiet resolve is what gets you in the door.

week 3.verse line: I started this with determination, and determination will carry me to the end.
You are made of what you deeply believe. As your faith is, so are you.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have spent eight months looking, and now your own nature has shown you the way forward. Your faith in what is right for you is becoming your reality.

week 3.verse line: Pleasant or painful, meet whatever comes with a heart that refuses to be defeated.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have been waiting eight months for this letter. Now that it has arrived, meet the day with a heart that knows it can hold whatever comes next.

week 3.verse line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
week 3.personal line written for them: The offer letter is the fruit of your own effort, and this turning is the proof. Let the timing be what it is, and keep going.

week 3.verse line: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, a great letter-go. Drop your doubts and hold steady.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have found your footing, and now you can act with full force. Enjoy this turning, and let it steady you.

week 3.verse line: Rein in the rush of anger and of excitement alike, and keep your head in trouble.
week 3.personal line written for them: You have turned a corner and want to keep the good moving. Hold the win without letting it rush you, and keep your head clear as you step forward.

week 3.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no...
week 3.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.
week 3.personal line written for them: Your offer letter is your brief. Keep your footing there and let the noise fall. Let the work move forward and let the insults fall.

person.their note: My granddaughter was born on Tuesday. Both of them are healthy. I just want to say thank you to someone.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I want to feel more grateful

week 1.verse line: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.
week 1.personal line written for them: The searching you feel now is the space where small offerings become enough. A grandparent's quiet morning, a grandchild's call, the warmth of a cup of tea. These are the leaves and water you are being asked to offer.

week 1.verse line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have walked over your own inner life for decades, never knowing it was a treasure. The search for what it is all for is not about finding a new path, but about seeing the ground you are already standing on.

week 1.verse line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have carried a long life and now you are looking for a deeper ground to stand on. You are not broken, but you are searching, and that is a hard place to be. You do not need to build a new self.

week 1.verse line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
week 1.personal line written for them: You are looking at a day that offers no grand answers, only the quiet arrival of a meal without humiliation and the space to breathe. In the middle of your family's worry, this freedom to sit still is the treasure you have been walking over.

week 1.verse line: Put the effort you spend earning money into growing wiser first.
week 1.personal line written for them: The effort you once put into earning a living can now go into growing wiser. You do not need to leave your life to find what you are looking for. You can sit with your family and let your mind rest. Let your own company be enough.

week 1.verse line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have stepped back from the daily earning, the way the verse says. Now the work is to see the life you have lived in the people around you. Your grandchild carries something of you forward, and your family holds the shape of your years.

week 1.story: The proud ascetic, the housewife and the butcher
week 1.summary: A young ascetic who can burn a bird with a glance is humbled by a housewife who knows what he did, and she sends him to a butcher in the market for teaching. The butcher, doing his trade honestly and caring for his parents, teaches him the highest truth. Doing the duty in front of you, without...
week 1.lesson: No honest work is beneath you; doing it well is the practice.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have spent a life doing things, and now the doing has stopped. This story says the search for a deeper life is not about finding a new grand purpose, but about bringing the same honest care to the small tasks that remain.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: You want to hold on to this feeling, and this verse says a mind without strain is a grace that comes to those whom Hari is pleased to bless.

week 1.verse line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding a new life in your hands, and the peace that comes with it is its own reward. Let this quiet gratitude be the blessing you count today.

week 1.verse line: We act only when we find joy in it. Understand the joy, and action follows.
Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are holding a new life. The verse says that undivided devotion is met with being carried and guarded. Let this gratitude be your offering today.

week 1.verse line: Always first learn to be a servant, and then you will be fit to be a master.
Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
week 1.personal line written for them: The joy of your granddaughter is a gift you can offer back. Let this gratitude shape the small acts of your day.

week 1.verse line: Drop your timidity. Keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
week 1.personal line written for them: You hold a new life in your heart, and you want to keep this warmth close. As his messengers, you have found your way. Let this gratitude be your way forward today.

week 1.story: Ram cannot repay Hanuman
week 1.summary: Back from Lanka, Hanuman tells Ram how Sita survives: his name guards her day and night. Ram, in tears, asks whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers that the only calamity is forgetting him. Ram says he can never repay Hanuman and cannot even look him in the face;...
week 1.lesson: Do the work, give away the credit, and ask only to keep loving.
week 1.personal line written for them: You want to hold on to this joy, and the verse asks you to give the credit away. Let the thank you flow toward the source that made this possible.

person.their note: I have been sitting quietly for ten minutes each morning for a month. It is good. I want to go deeper.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: Your calm steadiness is a quiet engine for the work you are building.

week 1.verse line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
Without inner discipline there's no clarity; without clarity, no peace; and without peace, where is happiness?
Ponds fill drop by drop. Good qualities gather in a person the same way.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your ten minutes of morning quiet have already begun to gather. The stillness you are finding is deepening, drop by drop.

week 1.verse line: The world is a grand moral gymnasium wherein we have all to take exercise so as to become stronger and stronger spiritually.
Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your quiet mornings have become a steady home. Let them deepen at their own pace. The mind knows how to settle when it is trusted.

week 1.verse line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.

week 1.story: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
week 1.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
week 1.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
week 1.personal line written for them: You have been returning to the quiet each morning. That patient return is already bringing you closer to what you are.

plan_B.first words shown with Day 1: I want a calm start to my day

week 1.verse line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind keeps running because it was never taught to stop. It is not a flaw. It is a habit of work and worry that has no switch. You do not need to push it down. You could come to rest little by little, with patience.

week 1.verse line: When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are working with a mind that keeps chasing what is next, and that is exactly what Krishna describes. The restlessness you feel is not a lack of will. It is the wind taking the boat.

week 1.verse line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind moves from one restless thought to the next because it is looking for a solid ground that is not there, and that ground is not in any passing feeling. The work is not to stop the weather, but to know that the sky remains.

week 1.verse line: Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm: that's the food of a clear mind.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your mind is restless because it is being fed noise. It is trying to digest things that do not build life. Choose what you take in this morning. Let it be simple and true. Let your mind eat something that creates calm.

week 1.verse line: If you can't keep your mind fixed yet, then reach for it through regular practice.
week 1.personal line written for them: Your work has trained you to solve, to move, to fix. But the mind that will not settle asks for a different kind of work, one that returns each day. The verse does not ask you to force stillness. It asks you to return.

week 1.verse line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are looking for a calm start, but the mind that won't settle is still a mind that is moving. The work you do each day is already keeping the body alive, and it is also the ground where a clear mind can begin.

week 1.story: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
week 1.summary: Thanking Krishna for dispelling his confusion, Arjuna asks to see his imperishable form if he is able.
week 1.lesson: Ask humbly for what you long to see.
week 1.personal line written for them: The mind that would not settle asked for a vision of everything. Now you are left with the ordinary morning, the inbox, the quiet before the day. That is where your part is. You do not need to see the whole picture to begin.

person.their note: UPSC prelims in May. I have a timetable and this time I am going to follow it.

plan_A.first words shown with Day 1: I can't stay consistent

week 1.verse line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are not lazy. You are stuck and not starting. The work that is yours is right in front of you. The next step is yours to take.

week 1.verse line: Six habits block every rise: oversleeping, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
week 1.personal line written for them: You are sitting with your books and the doubt is louder than the page. That is the pattern. The verse names it as one of the six faults that block every rise, not as a flaw in you. Decide calmly. Act steadily. That is your part right now.

week 1.verse line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
week 1.personal line written for them: You want to study and you know the work is yours. Let your friends praise or blame your habits. Let money come or go. The steady do not step off the right path.

week 1.verse line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
